rulings.why: Unchanged code can only show the symptom [1, 0] again: the check keeps no state (test-engineer F7). D-1's two counters tell the cause apart from a real defect. over_at_write above 0 would be a real overflow at a write. rulings.ruling: Keep held_grew, check_held_falls and both held_grew asserts. This is required, not optional.

G-NC2's loop exit needs beyond > 0, which is now set only at writes, so G-NC2 hits its 30 s hang guard (delay_tests.rs:38, :2283). That is two independent failures. A count would add a field and asserts and prove nothing more.

The bound holds by construction at every write (F7), derived independently: free_budget = 64 KB − (write_seq − snd_una) (tcp_model.rs:2211-2214); model_end == write_seq (write_seq starts at 0, :600; it moves only in write, :2221); admission n+22 <= free_budget − released_model (delay.rs:473-484, :1561-1572, :803); released_model falls only when a record is taken whole (:1510, :1761); step_to harvests at every event (:618-641) and model.write's own advance(now) is a no-op at both sites (tcp_model.rs:2218; delay.rs:1571, :1813-1815). So held <= 64 KB + prefix at each write, both ways.

Between writes the bound falls only at a release (harvest :675-696) while held stays unchanged. Over-samples are therefore only the release transient, never at a write. G-NC2's only sample outside a write is the pump's closing block (:1879); poll_write's :1594 cannot trip (F10).
